title: Bram and the Machine
premise: Emrys Coldharbour, a clone of a murdered shipping magnate, has spent ten years hiding in the margins of contested space as a cargo hauler. When the manifest of the Meridian's Wake—a ship officially scrapped before it ever flew—lists her under an unfamiliar name, she is pulled into an investigation of the Kestrel Reach massacre, an event erased from every official record. As she uncovers that her original was killed to bury the massacre, and that the erasure machine itself is still hunting loose ends like her, Emrys must choose between vanishing again and forcing the truth into the light. In the end, she broadcasts the evidence through the jump relay seconds before the window closes, sacrificing her anonymity forever but winning justice for the dead and, at last, a name and community that are truly her own.
about_author: Zephyrine Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime logistics analyst who spent six years coordinating freight contracts in high-risk ports before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about people the systems were built to overlook, and live quietly somewhere with unreliable internet on purpose.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys hauls scrap through contested orbits, invisible by design, until a routine customs scan flags her name on the manifest of the Meridian's Wake—a ship destroyed eleven years ago, before it ever launched. The beat is unease: her careful invisibility has cracked for reasons she can't see.

chapters.title: The Name That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She traces the manifest entry to a broker named Ovid Sarn, who claims he never filed it—and shows her the ship's registry: it lists a full crew of forty, all officially 'never employed.' Emotional beat: dread hardening into curiosity as Emrys realizes someone wanted this paper trail found.

chapters.title: Kestrel Reach
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Digging into the Wake's last logged heading, she finds only a void where the mining station Kestrel Reach should be—no wreckage, no records, no memorial. An old dockhand lets slip that people used to talk about it, then stopped. Beat: the chill of a hole cut cleanly out of history.

chapters.title: Ten Years a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Emrys in flashback. We learn how she inherited the original Coldharbour's identity, his unsolved murder case, and his enemies—how she learned that clones inherit debts, not protections. Beat: grief and self-erasure; she built her small life as armor, and now remembers why.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A stranger named Ilsa Vane boards at Ceres Junction claiming to be a records auditor, but asks questions about Kestrel Reach with too much precision. Emrys lies well enough to survive the encounter. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve—the erasure has a face now, and it's looking for her.

chapters.title: Forty Names
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Sarn decrypts a fragment of the Wake's true manifest: forty crew, hired in secret, bound for Kestrel Reach three days before the station 'never existed.' One name matches a woman living openly two jumps away. Beat: hope—the first witness who might still be breathing.

chapters.title: The Widow of Halcyon Drift
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She finds Mara Okonkwo, listed as the Wake's navigator, now running a noodle bar and pretending very hard to be nobody. Mara slams the door on her. Beat: frustration and recognition—two women who chose the same survival strategy, one of them refusing to break it.

chapters.title: What the Station Saw
chapters.summary: POV Mara (first departure from Emrys). Mara relives the night corporate security forces boarded Kestrel Reach and the Wake's crew was ordered to fly away and forget. She didn't see the killings—but she saw the ships, the timestamps, the orders. Beat: guilt; she saved herself by agreeing to disappear.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Mara offers a deal: her testimony and a data shard from the Wake's black box, in exchange for Emrys getting it out before Vane's employers scrub the last witnesses—including both of them. Beat: reluctant alliance; trust extended cautiously across old wounds.

chapters.title: Black Box Blues
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The shard is encrypted with a key tied to the original Emrys Coldharbour's biometrics—which means Emrys herself may be the only key left. But accessing it pings the network, and within hours Vane's ship changes course toward them. Beat: the trap tightens; her inheritance becomes either salvation or beacon.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Evidence
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Using her original's biometric signature, she cracks the shard: flight recordings, casualty lists, and a corporate directive authorizing 'site remediation' at Kestrel Reach. Her original had been gathering this when he was murdered. Beat: fury and purpose—the case she inherited finally has its shape.

chapters.title: Vane Comes Calling
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vane. Inside the antagonist's head: Vane isn't a zealot but a professional who erases atrocities for a fee, and she genuinely believes some truths cost more than they're worth. She offers Emrys money, a new identity, a clean disappearance. Beat: chilling reasonableness; temptation offered politely.

chapters.title: The Price of Vanishing
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Vane's offer forces the question Emrys has dodged for ten years: what is her invisibility actually for? She almost takes the deal—until she reads the casualty list again and finds children among the names. Beat: crisis of identity; she realizes she's been hiding from her own life.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She turns Vane down and goes dark, but Vane anticipated it: Sarn is taken, Mara's bar burns, and the jump relay that could broadcast the evidence will be sealed after the next window closes in six days. Beat: despair and commitment—retreat is no longer possible, only forward.

chapters.title: Assembly of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys rallies the scattered survivors of the erasure: two more Wake crew, a Kestrel Reach widow, a disgraced registrar who falsified the ship's death certificate under duress. Beat: belonging—for the first time, she stands inside a community instead of outside every one.

chapters.title: The Registrar's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Dell Hargrove, the registrar. He explains how the record-scrubbing machine works—an AI system called LACUNA that rewrites archives wholesale—and, crucially, that it cannot edit anything already mid-transmission through an open jump relay. Beat: the plan crystallizes around a single narrow door in time.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The team prepares: testimony recorded, evidence packaged, routes scouted past Vane's blockade of the relay approach. Old grudges flare between survivors who made different bargains with silence. Beat: rising tension and friction—unity forged under pressure, not given.

chapters.title: Running the Blockade
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The run for the relay: Emrys pilots her battered hauler through Vane's picket line while Mara jams their tracking and Hargrove rides shotgun with the evidence core. Beat: pure momentum—ten years of caution burned in ninety minutes of speed.

chapters.title: LACUNA Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Vane triggers LACUNA directly, and the machine begins rewriting not just records but the relay's targeting data—turning the infrastructure itself against them. Emrys realizes the enemy was never one woman but a system designed so no one is ever guilty. Beat: the stakes become existential.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Emrys, climax. With minutes left in the jump window, Emrys uploads everything—the massacre footage, the forty names, the directive, her own testimony as a clone who inherited the crime—into the open relay, unstoppable once transmitted. Vane's ship closes in; the transmission completes as boarding clamps lock on. Beat: triumph purchased at the price of safety.

chapters.title: Accounting
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Detained but untouchable—her evidence is everywhere—Emrys watches the fallout ripple outward: investigations reopened, executives indicted, LACUNA exposed and dismantled piece by piece. Vane, facing her own employers' cleanup protocols, chooses to testify. Beat: justice arriving imperfectly but undeniably, outside any court she'd trusted.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. At the first public memorial for Kestrel Reach, the forty names read aloud include the crew the records denied. Mara reopens her bar as a gathering place; the survivors claim Emrys as family—not as Coldharbour's copy, but as herself. Beat: resolution and belonging; she keeps her name, and it finally means something she chose.
